title: engineering-all-hands-2026-05-27
content:
Attendees: cross-org engineering, product leads, SRE, applied-ML, developer-experience

Overview
- Quick sync covering platform health, recent incidents, deliverables shipped this week, and upcoming milestones. Focus this week: autoscaler hardening, serving-runtime quantized path improvements, and rollout plan for private VPC control plane beta.

Highlights / Wins
- Serving-runtime: merged quantization-friendly kernel selection (PR #567) into main. Early internal perf tests show ~1.4x throughput improvement for 8-bit workloads on A10G with minimal regression on 16-bit paths. Thanks to the runtime and applied-ML teams for coordinated bench runs.
- Dedicated: completed first end-to-end smoke test of Dedicated burst capacity for a multi-tenant customer; validated billing telemetry and quota enforcement. Customer on-boarding checklist updated.
- Observability: Console now exposes per-route token cost breakdown in staging; this unblocks the next internal demo with growth next week.

Operational / Incidents
- May 20 partial serving degradation (SLA impact window ~40m) root cause: autoscaler experienced thrashing due to simultaneous cold-starts and a bug in the cooldown timer (ENG-4821). Mitigation: rolled back cooldown change and applied emergency fix (hotfix branch merged). Postmortem draft linked in artifacts. Action items: add additional safety windows to autoscaler logic, add unit tests for cooldown behavior, and create a chaos test in CI that simulates burst cold starts.
- Current platform uptime: 99.95% (last 30 days). P99 latency for text generation (hosted API): 560ms; avg token throughput: 8.9M tokens/day. We saw a 7% increase in token demand week-over-week driven by one large customer test.

Team updates (short bullets from subteams)
- Serving-runtime (Samir): working on KV cache garbage collection to reduce memory spikes; investigating small regression in batching latency for short sequences. Roadmap: deliver continuous-batching improvement by mid-June.
- Private Deployments (Elena): private VPC control plane beta on track for limited customers next week; finishing docs for on-prem install checklist. Need SRE runbook verification.
- Observability (Priya): adding distributed trace correlation across model fallsbacks; dashboard refresh scheduled for staging Friday.
- Release Engineering (Michael): prepping release pipeline change to support multi-arch images (x86 + ARM) for Private; will require new canary gating in staging.
- SRE (Kumail): incident response drill scheduled June 3; focus on multi-region failover and config rollback.

Roadblocks / Risks
- Autoscaler: remaining risk around spin-up times for certain GPU types - need capacity simulation and more conservative fallbacks while the new cooldown logic is validated.
- Private beta adoption: packaging/installer size and customer firewall rules are tripping a few early adopters. Engineering to provide a lightweight troubleshooting container and a sample allowed-ports matrix.
- Hiring: infra SWE hiring remains a bottleneck for Q3 roadmap - growth and recruiting to prioritize senior infra candidates.

Decisions / Asks
- Approve temporary throttle on new large burst onboarding until autoscaler cooldown fixes are fully tested (vote: +9 / -1 / 2 abstain). Outcome: throttle approved for two weeks.
- Observability agreed to prioritize per-route cost exposure for the top 10 customers next sprint.

Action Items (owners + due dates)
- Samir: KV cache GC design doc and prototype (due 2026-06-10).
- Elena + SRE: finalize private VPC runbook and firewall troubleshooting container (due 2026-06-03).
- Priya: push per-route token cost dashboard to staging and prepare demo (due 2026-05-31).
- Release Eng (Michael): enable multi-arch canary gating in staging and coordinate test matrix (due 2026-06-07).
- Platform leadership: schedule postmortem review session for the May 20 autoscaler incident (meeting invite for 2026-05-29).

Meeting notes / Q&A highlights
- Q: Will the quantization improvements affect API contracts? A: No API changes; model variant naming remains the same. We will expose the quantization profile in the model metadata.
- Q: Can customers opt out of autoscaler behavior? A: We will add an "autoscale: off" config for Dedicated reserved pools, but it will be limited to private/dedicated tiers with clear capacity guarantees.
- Q: Timeline for Private GA? A: Goal is late Q3 for GA; beta customers will provide feedback through June.

Appendix / Links
- Postmortem draft: ENG-4821
- Quantization PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/567
- Platform roadmap Q2: https://confluence.redwoodinternal.org/display/ENG/Platform+Roadmap+Q2+2026

Notes to self (informal)
- Follow up with Growth about the one large customer's spike - is it an AB test or an integration?
- Check on CI time cost for the new chaos test; may need quota bump for k8s clusters.

Next all-hands: 2026-06-03 (same time).
